summary.whatItDoes: A lightweight Python utility that converts files such as PDF, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, images, audio, HTML, CSV/JSON/XML, ZIP files, YouTube URLs and EPubs into Markdown, aimed at LLM and text-analysis pipelines rather than high-fidelity human-readable conversion.
intendedUsers: Developers building LLM or RAG pipelines that need document text
People who want a command-line tool to turn documents into Markdown
learningOpportunities: See how one API (convert) can route many file types to format-specific converters.
Learn why Markdown is a token-efficient intermediate format for LLM input.
Read the Security Considerations section to understand the risks of converting untrusted inputs.

smallExperiment.title: Convert one of your own PDFs and compare the Markdown
steps: Create a fresh Python virtual environment as described in the README.
Install the package with pip install 'markitdown[all]'.
Run markitdown on a PDF you created yourself and redirect the output to a .md file.
Compare headings, lists and tables in the Markdown against the original document.

caveats: The README says it performs I/O with the privileges of the current process; do not pass untrusted inputs to it directly.
Output is meant for text-analysis tools and may not suit high-fidelity conversion for people.
LLM image descriptions require your own OpenAI-compatible client and incur that provider's costs.
